You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

description: Use when closed color borders enclose regions to fill.
---

# Fill enclosed cavities inside color borders

## Continual-ARC task-eb4783cc: closed frames take size-dependent fills (2026-09-30)

Two demos establish the following rule for the recurring decorated-frame task. Preserve grid and frame borders; fill only the enclosed interiors of closed square outlines, with fill color dependent on the interior area:
- Interior area 1 (1x1): fill 7.
- Interior area 4 (2x2): fill 2.
- Interior area 9 (3x3): fill 7.
- Interior area 16 (4x4): fill 2.
Thus fill 7 for odd-sized square interiors, and 2 for even-sized square interiors (sizes tested 1–4); do not use the frame color or neighboring shape to select the fill.

Evidence: demo 1 had 4x4 interiors of colors 4 and 3 both filled 2; a 2x2 interior of color 6 filled 2; 3x3 interior of color 5 filled 7; and 1x1 interior of color 1 filled 7. Demo 2 independently confirmed: 2x2 interior in color-8 frame filled 2; 5x5 interior in color-4 frame filled 7 (here the interior is 5x5, area 25; this supports odd width / odd side); singleton cavity in color-5 and color-1 frames both filled 7; and the large 5x5 rectangular interior in frame4 filled 7. The reliable interpretation is parity of the interior side length/area: odd side ->7, even side ->2. Test solved after two failed guesses when applying this criterion: color3 frame interior 4x4->2; color5 frame interior2x2->2; color4 frame interior1x1->7; color1 frame interior4x4->2; color6 frame interior1x1->7. Important: only fill enclosed interior cells, retain frame outlines and exterior unchanged.

Careful caveat: Demo2's large frame4 interior is 5 rows x 5 cols (not square's parity area narrative, but both side lengths odd); rule appears odd/even side length, not a fixed size lookup. The concise reusable rule is fill 7 when both interior dimensions are odd and 2 when both are even, as tested on square cavities; for non-square cases, request more evidence.


## Continual-ARC task-6c4b1169: verified rule and new recurrence

Preserve dimensions, original outline pixels, background, and exterior cells; change only background cells enclosed by complete monochrome outline loops to color 4. Use four-way connectivity/exterior reachability; do not fill open linework or merely bbox interiors unless truly enclosed. Background and outline colors vary; fill color 4 is fixed.

Fresh accepted test: 25x12, background 6, motif color 9. The closed rectangle-like loop is rows 18–24, cols 2–4, enclosing exactly cells (19,3),(20,3),(21,3),(22,3),(23,3); recolor all five to 4. Preserve the outline, including row21’s gap at c3 (that enclosed cell becomes 4), and all exterior cells. Accepted after two wrong submissions: earlier guesses filled only r19-20 c3, or r19-20 plus r22-23 c3, both incomplete.

Fresh demos: (1) 23x13 bg5, outline2: contour encloses cells r18-20,c4-5, all six changed to4; unrelated bars unchanged. (2) 24x11 bg6, outline0: closed loop r3-7,c6-8 encloses (4,7),(5,7),(6,7); another loop r10-12,c5-8 encloses (11,6),(11,7); exactly these five cells change to4. (3) 24x10 bg9, outline3: loop r0-4,c0-5 encloses r1-3,c1-4 (12 cells); another closed irregular loop encloses r7-10,c1-3 (12 cells); fill only cavities.

Prior records also support this topological fill rule, including accepted test bg1/outline7 with cavities rows18-21 cols4-7 and cols16-17 filled 4. Beware old coordinate summaries can be inconsistent; derive bounds from each live grid. First verify closure and cavity pixels, then recolor the enclosed background. Do not confuse open boundary bars with closed outlines.

Rule: preserve dimensions, background, and outline pixels; fill enclosed cavities of closed color-2 outlines with color 4. The background and frame colors may vary; output fill is 4. In the 9x23 test (background 0), the closed outline occupies rows 2-5, cols 3-6, with its 2x2 interior at rows 2-4? Exact filled cells were (r2,c4-5), (r3,c4-5), and (r4,c4-5); accepted output confirms these six cells changed from 0 to 4. Preserve all other cells, including open/incomplete linework elsewhere.

Demo evidence: 8x9, bg0, 2-outline rectangle rows1-3 cols1-3 encloses 2x2 interior rows1-2 cols1-2; output changes these four cells to 4 only. 25x18, bg6, enclosed areas in the lower motif selectively fill with 4, leaving open or external 2-shapes unchanged. 24x24, bg5, 6-outline frame around rows8-11 cols15-19 encloses interior rows8-10 cols16-18; fill those 3x3 cells with 4 only. This supports topological enclosed-background flood-fill rather than filling every region inside a visually suggestive bbox: determine exterior via four-way connectivity, and change only enclosed background cells.


For task-6c4b1169, locate continuous, closed outlines/frames and recolor only their enclosed interior/background cells to 4. Keep the outline pixels and all exterior/background cells unchanged. Use four-way connectivity to determine whether a background region can reach the grid's exterior without crossing the outline; only non-exterior cavities are filled. The frame and background colors vary, while fill color 4 is fixed.

Verified evidence:
- Demo: 17x26 grid with background 9 and outline color 0. The output fills the interior of closed outlines with 4 while preserving every outline pixel and all exterior cells. One filled cavity spans rows 7-12, columns 13-16; another small enclosed area appears at rows 9-11, column 6.
- Test: 29x19 grid with background 1 and outline color 7. Correct output fills only the enclosed areas: rows 18-21, columns 4-7, and rows 18-21, columns 16-17, with 4. Preserve the outline at rows 17-22 and all exterior cells. This was accepted after one incorrect attempt.
